title: Mileage and engine hours each carry their own confidence
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Maintenance Reminders QA build as an Owner/Admin (any user who can open Settings > Maintenance and create and edit work orders and customers).
  2. Open Settings > Maintenance, press New schedule and create a throwaway schedule 'ZZAUTOTEST Reading seed' holding one routine service per reading you will seed, named 'ZZ Seed 1', 'ZZ Seed 2' and so on, each with a Calendar trigger of Every 12 months and no canned lines. Save. (If it already exists, reuse it.)
  3. In Settings > Maintenance create a schedule 'ZZAUTOTEST Rate PM' with one service 'PM-M': a Distance trigger set At 360,000 mileage and a Calendar trigger of Every 12 months. Save.
  4. Open Customers > 'ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Co' > Assets and create unit 'ZZAUTOTEST 564' with New Asset, leaving Mileage and Engine Hours empty. On its Maintenance tab press Enroll in Schedule, choose 'ZZAUTOTEST Reading seed' and give every seed service a last service date five years ago (for example 6 Oct 2021), so each seed service reads Overdue and shows on the work order card; press Enroll. Enroll the unit on 'ZZAUTOTEST Rate PM' too, with PM-M last done today.
  5. Readings for 'ZZAUTOTEST 564' (oldest first): 1) 18 Jul 2026 · 296,000 mileage · 6,000 engine hours; 2) 28 Jul 2026 · 297,000 mileage · 6,100 engine hours; 3) 16 Sep 2026 · 302,000 mileage; 4) 26 Sep 2026 · 303,000 mileage. Dates are for a run on 6 Oct 2026. On another day, move every date by the same number of days and seed and read on the same day, because an estimate and a reading's age both count days up to today.
  6. Seed each reading in the table, oldest first: open Work Orders and press New Work Order for the unit; type the reading's mileage in the work order's Mileage field (and its engine hours in Engine Hours where the table gives one; leave the field untouched where it does not) and save; expand the Maintenance schedule card, open the three-dot menu of a seed service not used yet, choose Mark complete, keep On a work order with this work order chosen, set Reset date to the reading's date and press Mark complete. That work order's values become readings dated the Reset date. Confirm any warning the field shows.
  7. When every reading is in: on the unit's Maintenance tab open the 'ZZAUTOTEST Reading seed' schedule's menu, choose Remove from schedule and confirm, so the seed services add no rows. Check the Mileage card's last recorded value and date match the table's last reading.
custom_steps:
1. Open unit 564's Maintenance tab and read the confidence on the Mileage card and on the Engine hours card.
  2. Hover the (i) beside the Engine hours card's Current estimate and read it.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Mileage: three usable pairs, the last reading 10 days old → High.
  • Engine hours: one pair (the hours were typed on the first two work orders only), the last reading 70 days old → Low.
  • The two grades differ because each meter is graded on its own readings.
  • The (i) says the engine hours estimate is the same calculation (in the design: “The same calculation, run against the hour meter.”).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10568 (S11, Rate, estimate and confidence); Chunk 2 MR (Confluence 897679389) as edited 5 October 2026, S11; Design MR_V2_2 (Claude Design export, 6 Oct 2026), driven in full on 6 Oct 2026, Chunk 1 board artboards S4 / X1t; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S11-R10: “Distance and engine hours will each carry their own confidence, computed independently”
  • S10-N6: “A reading on a work order counts only when someone entered or changed the value on that work order”
  • S18-R19: “Mark complete On a work order also records that work order's mileage and engine hours as the asset's readings, dated the Reset date”
  • Design, Chunk 1 board, artboards S4 / X1t, (i) beside the Engine hours estimate: “The same calculation, run against the hour meter.”
